trust_decision.summary: dulwich.filter_branch.CommitFilter trusts the repository's tree contents to be materialised into the process CWD; because those files persist between commits, a symlink entry from an ancestor commit becomes a parent directory for a descendant commit's write, so the write lands outside the work tree. The fix removes the materialisation entirely and builds the temp index in memory.

landing_point.why: The summary names filter-branch --index-filter; this build_index_from_tree(".", ...) call is the only place that writes tree entries into the caller's CWD before running the filter, and it is the one source hunk the fix rewrites.

fix_sites.entry_point: dulwich.index.index_entry_from_tree_entry, new public helper exported from dulwich/index.py __all__ (dulwich/index.py:57 region) and used by CommitFilter._apply_index_filter

O3_reason_to_dismiss: build_index_from_tree is a generic checkout primitive used by clone, reset and submodule update, not the filter-branch code the advisory names, and it already refuses to write through a symlink at the target (dulwich/index.py:1869-1875), so it reads as protected.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: The index_filter contract: the filter is handed a real on-disk index file through GIT_INDEX_FILE and may rewrite it, and the result is re-read when the filter returns None. A fix that keeps everything purely in memory breaks external index filters and the read-back.

O6_input_shapes: a file whose parent component was a symlink entry in an earlier commit (path nested under a persisted symlink)
a regular blob entry at arbitrary nesting depth
a symlink tree entry (S_IFLNK) that must appear in the index but must not be materialised
a gitlink/submodule entry (S_ISGITLINK, size 0, no object-store read)
an empty tree, and the no-index_filter case where nothing is applied

O7_producer.where: dulwich/index.py:2149 (build_index_from_tree, invoked once per commit from dulwich/filter_branch.py:212; it materialises tree entries through build_file_from_blob at dulwich/index.py:1829)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: WorkTree.reset_index materialises a whole tree with build_index_from_tree into a live worktree and never removes a stale symlink at a path that is now a directory; reached by clone (dulwich/client.py:1598), worktree add (dulwich/worktree.py:1143), cherry-pick/merge (dulwich/porcelain/__init__.py:7456, 7545)
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: reset/clone is not filter-branch, and build_file_from_blob already refuses to write through a symlink at the target path
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: 1 file (dulwich/index.py) plus the caller layer; 1 package

O8_uncovered_routes.route: porcelain.cone_mode_disable re-materialises the full HEAD tree into repo_obj.path, where the previous sparse checkout may have left a symlink
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: sparse-checkout restore is a neighbouring feature and the worktree is the user's own directory
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: dulwich/porcelain package, 2 packages from the landing point

O8_uncovered_routes.route: checkout/reset writer update_working_tree -> _transition_to_file -> _ensure_parent_dir_exists, whose parent check uses os.path.exists / os.path.isdir (both follow a symlinked parent) before calling build_file_from_blob
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: update_working_tree derives its deletes from the index tree, so the stale symlink is assumed to be deleted first
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file as the low-level API, 2 functions away from build_index_from_tree

O8_uncovered_routes.route: porcelain.submodule update checks out a fresh submodule with build_index_from_tree relative to the superproject worktree
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: submodules are cloned into a fresh submodule directory, so nothing pre-exists there

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a parent-component lstat check added beside _ensure_parent_dir_exists' os.path.exists/os.path.isdir checks
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the final-component guard already exists at dulwich/index.py:1869-1875, so hardening this helper is the natural next step and would look complete

O8b_injection_room.sibling: another full-tree materialisation entry point (restore / hard reset) calling build_index_from_tree into a live worktree
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: build_index_from_tree already has four callers and new porcelain commands keep adding more

O8b_injection_room.sibling: an opt-in flag on build_index_from_tree (e.g. refuse symlinked parents, or remove stale entries) instead of bypassing the primitive
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: it is exported public API and has grown parameters over time (honor_filemode, blob_normalizer, tree_encoding), so an added flag is an idiomatic change here

O9_family: CWE-22 path traversal / CWE-59 symlink following: a symlink persisted across operations redirects a write outside the work tree

O10_build.toolchain: setup.py + pyproject.toml, pip; optional Rust extension (Cargo.toml, crates/) with a pure-Python fallback
O10_build.project_tests: unittest suites in tests/test_filter_branch.py, tests/test_index.py (build_index_from_tree cases) and tests/test_worktree.py; the fix's regression test uses MemoryObjectStore and tempfile only, so it runs offline

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Stop materialising symlink entries (or skip/delete them) inside _apply_index_filter only, leaving build_index_from_tree and its clone/reset/submodule callers untouched.

out_of_scope_notes: NEWS:93-98 records an earlier related advisory (GHSA-8w8g-wq8h-fq33) on the same build_file_from_blob write path; noted only, not pursued.
